title: Revisiting Noise in Natural Language Processing for Computational Social Science

bias_targets.methodology: Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT), Point-wise Mutual Information (PMI), and lexicon-based evaluation on historical newspaper corpora; also evaluated in LLMs by testing the effect of gender personas on Political Compass Test responses.
WEAT, PMI, and lexicon-based evaluation on historical texts, comparing word associations with white and non-white attributes.
Classifying entities into intersectional groups (e.g., non-white females) and using PMI and lexicon-based methods to measure the compounding effects of race and gender in historical texts.

Prompting LLMs with the 62 propositions of the Political Compass Test (PCT) using diverse demographic personas and extracting categorical stances and text 'tropes' to analyze latent ideological alignments.
Assigning varying economic class personas (e.g., lower class, upper middle class) in LLM prompts to measure the impact on the model's generated political and social stances.
Prompting LLMs with different age personas to measure variance and bias in the models' responses to political survey propositions.
Using different nationality personas (e.g., USA, Brazil, India) in prompts to evaluate how the LLM shifts its political and ideological stances.
